name: Beastie Boys
hook: A New York hardcore punk band turned rap group, whose first album was the first rap album to top the US album chart and whose second was a landmark of sampling.
blurb: Adam Yauch (MCA), Mike Diamond (Mike D) and Adam Horovitz (Ad-Rock) started as a hardcore punk band in New York in 1981. Rick Rubin, who came from the same punk scene, helped them switch to rap, and they are filed under hip-hop because their defining work is inside that form (A120). Their first album, Licensed to Ill (1986), was the first rap album to reach number one on the US album chart. Its frat-boy persona and its sexism were things the group later rejected, in their own lyrics and in public statements. Their second, Paul's Boutique (1989), made with the Dust Brothers, was built from hundreds of samples, the densest sampling record of its moment. It sold badly at first but is now seen as one of the great sampling records, made two years before the Grand Upright ruling (see e-coldchillin-bizmarkie) would have made clearing that many samples ruinously expensive. The group ended when Adam Yauch died in 2012.
